title: When Is the Best Time of Year to Refinish Hardwood Floors in Edmonds?
meta: The best time to refinish hardwood floors in Edmonds is late spring or early fall, but heated homes refinish well year-round. Wills Flooring's month-by-month guide.
keywords: best time of year to refinish hardwood floors, refinish hardwood floors summer or winter, hardwood floor refinishing humidity, when to refinish floors Edmonds, hardwood refinishing Edmonds WA

blocks.lead: The best months to refinish hardwood floors in Edmonds are late April through June and September through mid-October: mild temperatures, moderate humidity, open windows, and a calendar that is not yet full.
blocks.detail: With the heat on and a water-based Bona finish, a refinish cures fine in January too, and winter dates are easier to book. The real deciding factors are your household schedule and the moisture in the house, not the month. Prices are the same year-round: $3.99 per sq ft natural, $6.50 with stain, $1.99 for a recoat.

blocks.html: Edmonds homeowners ask this more than people inland do, and for good reason. Houses in the Bowl and along Sunset Avenue sit in marine air that keeps humidity high most of the year. Seaview and Perrinville ramblers from the 1960s have crawlspaces that breathe that same damp air up through the floor. So the question behind the question is really: will the weather ruin my finish? It will not, if the job is planned around the conditions inside the house. Here is how each season actually behaves on a refinishing job in Edmonds, and how to pick a date that fits your life.

items.title: Humidity: the finish and the boards
items.text: Water-based finish dries by evaporation. Above about 60 percent indoor humidity, coats take longer between passes and can stay soft an extra day. Boards also swell in damp months and shrink in dry ones, so a floor sanded at its widest can show hairline gaps by February. Neither is a defect; it is timing.

items.title: Temperature: the cure
items.text: Finish wants the room between about 65 and 75 degrees. Edmonds rarely gets too hot; the risk is a cold house in winter when owners turn the heat down while they are out. Keep the furnace at normal living temperature for the whole job and the week after.

items.title: Ventilation and dust
items.text: Spring and fall let us crack windows for airflow between coats without pulling in pollen or wood-stove smoke. Summer brings open-window dust; deep winter means closed windows and slower off-gassing, so dust containment and an air scrubber earn their keep.

items.title: Daylight and color
items.text: Stain colors read differently in gray January light than in June. If you are choosing a stain, sample it in the season you will live with most. Low winter sun also shows sanding marks more clearly, which is one reason winter jobs need a careful final pass.

blocks.text: Pick the date around your life, then check the weather

items.text: Refinish in September or October, before the holidays and before the spring listing crush. The floor has months to settle and you can stage on it.

items.d: Young kids or a new baby
items.text: Book a week when you can stay elsewhere for three or four nights. Summer works if grandparents are nearby; a June job dries fast and the house airs out quickly.
items.note: Water-based finish is walkable in socks after 24 hours

items.d: Downsizing into a Bowl condo or older Edmonds house
items.text: Refinish before you move in, whatever the month. An empty house is the single biggest schedule and quality advantage, more than any season.
items.note: Empty homes often finish a day sooner

items.text: Floors come after drywall, paint and cabinets, before baseboards and appliances. Let the remodel set the month; just keep the heat on once the finish goes down.

blocks.text: Edmonds moisture: the one factor that outranks the calendar

blocks.title: Check the crawlspace first:
blocks.text: A Seaview or Westgate rambler with a wet crawlspace and no vapor barrier will read high moisture in the floor in any month. Finish over damp boards can cloud, and boards sanded flat in a wet state can cup as they dry. We meter the wood at the estimate; if it reads high, fixing the crawlspace before sanding beats waiting for a dry season.
Times we tell Edmonds homeowners to wait

items.html: Right after a leak or flood. Boards need weeks to dry to normal readings before sanding. Refinishing a floor that is still drying locks in cupping. See refinishing water-damaged floors for what to expect.
The week the painters are in. Ladders and drips on fresh finish. Paint first, floors second, baseboards last.
Right before the house is closed up and unheated. A vacant home with the furnace off in December slows the cure and can leave the finish soft. Keep it at 65 or wait until someone is living there.
The week of a wood-stove heating stretch. Stove heat drives indoor humidity below 30 percent and boards shrink hard. Wait for a milder week, or run the furnace instead during the job.
Days before a party or listing photos. The finish is walkable in a day but fully hard in about a week. Give it that week before rugs, furniture and guests.

items: Check the indoor humidity with an inexpensive hygrometer for a week; 35 to 55 percent is the target, and a dehumidifier or the furnace fan can get you there.
Plan where the family and pets go for three to four days, plus the day of stain if you chose one.
Keep the heat at normal living temperature for the whole job and the following week, even if you are away.
Remove window coverings and screens that block airflow, and turn off forced-air returns in the work area if we ask.
Wait 72 hours before furniture and two to three weeks before area rugs so the finish cures evenly.
If you are choosing stain, look at samples in your own light in the season you care about most.

faq.q: Can hardwood floors be refinished in the winter in Edmonds?
faq.a: Yes. With the furnace holding a normal living temperature and a water-based finish, winter refinishing cures well and often dries faster than in humid months because indoor air is drier. The trade-off is closed windows, so we recommend dust containment and an air scrubber for occupied homes.

faq.q: Does Edmonds humidity ruin a hardwood floor finish?
faq.a: Not if the house is under control. Marine air keeps outdoor humidity high, but inside a heated, ventilated home readings usually sit in the 35 to 55 percent range that finish likes. The real risk is a damp crawlspace pushing moisture into the boards, which we meter before quoting.

faq.q: Is summer the best time to refinish hardwood floors?
faq.a: It is a good time for the finish and a hard time for the household. Warm, dry conditions cure coats quickly, but summer is our busiest season and families are home. Late spring and early fall give the same conditions with shorter waits and easier logistics.

faq.q: How long do refinished floors need to cure before I put furniture back?
faq.a: Walk in socks after 24 hours, light furniture after 72 hours, and wait two to three weeks before area rugs. Full hardness comes around a week in normal conditions; cold or very humid rooms can stretch that, which is why we ask you to keep the heat steady.

faq.q: Should I refinish before or after moving into my Edmonds home?
faq.a: Before, whenever you can. An empty house lets the crew work faster, sand every square foot without moving furniture, and keep the finish untouched while it cures. Empty homes often finish a day sooner, and the season matters far less than an open floor plan.

faq.q: Do refinishing prices change with the season?
faq.a: No. Wills Flooring's rates are the same all year: $3.99 per sq ft for a natural finish, $6.50 with stain, $1.99 for a screen and recoat, with a 500 sq ft minimum. What changes is how far out you need to book, from days in winter to weeks in summer.
